quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: For quick turns, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
At the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is safe and comfortable for turning.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red light after stopping?

options.text: You are on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.
You are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you can turn left at a red light only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street. Check for signs that prohibit this turn.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red light?

options.text: Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
Slow down and continue carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a full stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If your wheels go off the road edge, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then slowly steer back onto the road.
Turn back onto the road right away.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then slowly steer back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road immediately. Slow down, check traffic, and gradually steer back when it is safe.

questions.question: Your wheels go off the pavement edge. What is the first thing you should do?

options.text: Turn the wheel slightly left to edge the car back onto the pavement.
Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently brake.
Brake hard and turn the wheel sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently brake.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly, take your foot off the gas, and brake gently. Wait until you slow down, check traffic, and find a safe place to return to the road. Turning the wheel sharply can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: A car is tailgating you on a two-lane road. What should you do?

options.text: Slowly reduce your speed to let them pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake to slow down, then go back to your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce your speed to let them pass you.
questions.explanation: Move to another lane if you can. If not, slowly reduce your speed to encourage the tailgater to pass you.

questions.question: Which action should you never take when changing lanes?

options.text: Cross the center line in an intersection.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the center line in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Check for other drivers in your lane. Never change lanes in an intersection.

questions.question: What does a stop sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and stop if other cars are coming.
Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
Proceed carefully through the intersection without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the marked line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop where you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When can you turn left on a red light?

options.text: From a two-way road to a one-way road.
From a one-way road to a one-way road.
Except in school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: From a one-way road to a one-way road.
questions.explanation: You can turn left at a red light only from a one-way road to another one-way road (unless a sign says you cannot). Always stop and let other traffic and pedestrians pass first.

questions.question: When should you start slowing down to exit the highway?

options.text: Halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the speed posted for the exit ramp.

questions.question: When is turning and stopping most dangerous in rain?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars mixes with rain and creates a slippery coating on the road.

questions.question: How far behind a fire truck should you stay during an emergency?

options.text: At least 200 feet.
At least 500 feet.
Three to six seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 500 feet.
questions.explanation: Stay at least 500 feet behind a fire truck during an emergency. Stay at least 300 feet behind a police car during an emergency.

questions.question: When is the road most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain just begins.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain just begins.
questions.explanation: The road is most slippery when rain first starts. Dirt and oil on the road mix with the rain and create a slippery film.

questions.question: When passing another car, when should you move back to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the front bumper of the other car.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed car in your mirror. This means you have enough space to move back safely.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Brake lightly.
Do not use the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not brake. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?

options.text: Enter the far-right lane immediately and speed up to match traffic flow.
Use the shoulder of the main road to reach traffic speed.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic, then enter.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic before speeding up and entering. Stay stopped while waiting for a safe gap.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from an approaching car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the center line of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights from an oncoming vehicle. Then look ahead to track where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind while moving, press yourself against your seat and push your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it by following the rules.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What will the truck do?

options.text: Complete the turn using either of the two lanes.
Swing wide to complete the right turn.
Stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need to swing wide to make a right turn safely.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, which lane should you enter?

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: When turning, always turn from your lane into the first available legal lane. From a two-way street to a one-way street, this means entering the first lane.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Start signaling about 100 feet before the turn. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a railroad crossing.

options.text: 100 feet
75 feet
50 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. Park only in legal spots where other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: When should you increase your distance from the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: When should you give up your legal right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Yield whenever it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Continue at your regular speed.
Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the railroad tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for trains to pass before you proceed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down; curving road ahead.
Slow down and do not use your brakes.
Slow down; the road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down; the road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as for normal traffic violations.
You must slow down for the cone zone.
Slow down only if you think workers are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for the cone zone.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and be ready to slow or stop for highway equipment. Safe driving through work zones protects drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and workers.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, what is the safest way to drive?

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic (within posted limits). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: You want to pass a motorcycle. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and does not use the whole lane.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Be completely in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be completely in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give the motorcycle a full lane when passing. Never share a lane with a motorcycle. Returning to the right lane too soon can force the rider off the road.
